description: Master Tailwind CSS core concepts including utility-first design, mobile-first responsiveness, pseudo-classes, dark mode, and configuration.

slides.title: Introduction to Tailwind CSS
slides.content:
# Welcome to Tailwind CSS 💨

**Tailwind CSS** is a utility-first CSS framework packed with classes like `flex`, `pt-4`, `text-center`, and `rotate-90` that can be composed to build any design, directly in your markup.

## What Makes Tailwind Different?
- **No pre-designed components** — Unlike Bootstrap or MUI, Tailwind provides raw utility building blocks.
- **Work inside HTML** — No need to switch between HTML and CSS files constantly.
- **Zero unused CSS** — The Just-In-Time (JIT) compiler scans template files and generates only the exact CSS you use.
- **Consistent constraints** — Spacing scales, color palettes, and typography presets eliminate arbitrary pixel guesswork.

> 💡 **Key Mindset Shift:** Instead of naming CSS classes like `.user-profile-header-card`, you assemble visual primitives like `flex p-6 bg-white rounded-xl shadow-md`.

slides.title: The Utility-First Concept
slides.content:
# The Utility-First Architecture 🧱 In traditional CSS, you write custom semantic classes and associate styling rules in a stylesheet. In utility-first CSS, classes have single, focused responsibilities. ## Traditional CSS vs Utility-First | Aspect | Traditional CSS | Tailwind Utility-First | |---|---|---| | **Location** | Separate `.css` file | Directly in template markup | | **Class Naming** | Inventing names (`.author-bio-wrap`) | Standardized utilities (`flex`, `p-4`) | | **File Size** | Grows with every new feature | Hits a plateau (around 10-15kB gzipped) | | **Safety** | Changes risk breaking other elements | Modifying a component has zero side effects | ## Basic Component Example ```html_not
ChitChat

You have a new message!

``` > ⚡ **Advantage:** You never spend time coming up with meaningless class names like `wrapper`, `inner-container`, or `card-body-bottom`.

slides.title: Responsive Design & Mobile-First
slides.content:
# Responsive Design 📱💻 Tailwind uses an intuitive **mobile-first** breakpoint system. An un-prefixed utility applies to all screen sizes, while breakpoint-prefixed utilities apply at that breakpoint and above. ## Default Breakpoints | Prefix | Min-width | Typical Device Target | |---|---|---| | `sm:` | `640px` | Small tablets, landscape phones | | `md:` | `768px` | Tablets portrait/landscape | | `lg:` | `1024px` | Laptops and desktop displays | | `xl:` | `1280px` | Large desktop screens | | `2xl:` | `1536px` | Ultra-wide monitors | ## Mobile-First Example ```html_not
Card 1
Card 2
Card 3
Card 4
``` > ⚠️ **Crucial Rule:** Never write `sm:text-sm text-base` expecting `text-base` to apply on desktop! Write `text-sm md:text-base`.

slides.title: Targeting Ranges & Max Breakpoints
slides.content:
# Advanced Responsive Targeting 🎯 In modern Tailwind, you can also target max-width breakpoints or specific ranges using `max-*` modifiers. ## Max-Width Modifiers When you only want a style applied *below* a specific viewport size: ```html_not

Medium screen sidebar

``` ## Custom Breakpoints in Config ```javascript_not // tailwind.config.js module.exports = { theme: { screens: { 'tablet': '640px', 'laptop': '1024px', 'desktop': '1280px', }, }, }; ```

slides.title: Pseudo-Classes: Hover, Focus & Active
slides.content:
# Interactive States: Hover, Focus & Active 🖱️

Every Tailwind utility class can be conditionally applied on interactive states using state prefixes.

## Common Pseudo-Class Modifiers

| Modifier | Pseudo-Class | Common Use Cases |
|---|---|---|
| `hover:` | `:hover` | Button highlights, link underlines, card elevations |
| `focus:` | `:focus` | Input outlines, accessible keyboard rings |
| `active:` | `:active` | Button press effect (scale, color shift) |
| `focus-visible:` | `:focus-visible` | Keyboard-only accessibility outline |
| `disabled:` | `:disabled` | Dimmed opacity, `cursor-not-allowed` |

## Interactive Button Example

```html_not
<button class="bg-indigo-600 text-white font-medium px-5 py-2.5 rounded-lg
               hover:bg-indigo-700 active:scale-95
               focus:outline-none focus:ring-4 focus:ring-indigo-300
               disabled:opacity-50 disabled:cursor-not-allowed
               transition-all duration-200">
  Submit Form
</button>
```

slides.title: Group and Peer Modifiers
slides.content:
# Styling Based on Parent & Sibling State 👨‍👩‍👧 Tailwind provides `group` and `peer` modifiers to trigger styles when a parent or sibling changes state. ## 1. Group Modifier (`group-{modifier}`) Mark a parent with `group`, then style children based on parent hover or focus: ```html_not

Card Title

Subtitle changes text color on card hover!

→
``` ## 2. Peer Modifier (`peer-{modifier}`) Mark a previous sibling with `peer`, then style the following sibling: ```html_not

Please provide a valid email address.

``` > 📌 **Note:** `peer` only works with following siblings in the DOM tree.

Installation: CLI vs CDN
slides.content:
# Installation: Tailwind CLI vs Play CDN 📦

Depending on development vs production needs, Tailwind offers multiple setup routes.

## 1. Tailwind CLI (Recommended for Production)
Full performance with JIT compiling and minification:

```bash_not
# Install Tailwind CSS
npm install -D tailwindcss
npx tailwindcss init

# Start watch process
npx tailwindcss -i ./src/input.css -o ./dist/output.css --watch
```

## 2. Play CDN (For Prototyping Only)
Fastest setup with zero build tools, but downloads the whole JIT compiler in the browser:

```html_not
<script src="https://cdn.tailwindcss.com"></script>
<script>
  tailwind.config = {
    theme: {
      extend: {
        colors: { brand: '#da373d' }
      }
    }
  }
</script>
```

> ⚠️ **Warning:** Never use the Play CDN in production! It creates massive runtime overhead and lacks PostCSS optimizations.

slides.title: The Tailwind Configuration File
PostCSS Integration
slides.content:
# PostCSS Integration & Autoprefixer 🔌

In modern web build tools (Vite, Next.js, Webpack), Tailwind is typically integrated as a **PostCSS plugin**.

## `postcss.config.js` Setup

```javascript_not
module.exports = {
  plugins: {
    tailwindcss: {},
    autoprefixer: {},
  }
}
```

## Why PostCSS & Autoprefixer?
- **Automatic Vendor Prefixes**: PostCSS with Autoprefixer automatically adds browser prefixes like `-webkit-` and `-moz-` where necessary.
- **Seamless Bundler Integration**: Works natively with Vite, Astro, Webpack, Nuxt, and Remix.
- **Hot Module Replacement (HMR)**: Changes in classes instantly update the browser without full page reloads.

slides.title: Common Pitfalls & JIT Dynamic Classes
Summary & Best Practices Checklist
slides.content:
# Tailwind Basics: Summary Checklist 📋

Here is your roadmap for writing clean, efficient Tailwind CSS:

## Best Practices Checklist
- [x] **Embrace utility composition** — Build UI with utilities first; abstract to framework components (React/Vue) when repeating.
- [x] **Design mobile-first** — Un-prefixed classes for mobile, `sm:` / `md:` / `lg:` for wider viewports.
- [x] **Use complete strings** — Never interpolate dynamic substrings like `text-${size}`.
- [x] **Leverage state modifiers** — Use `hover:`, `focus:`, `group-hover:`, and `peer-invalid:` for rich interactions.
- [x] **Configure dark mode** — Choose `class` mode for user toggles and pair with `dark:` variants.
- [x] **Rely on Preflight** — Build on the standardized modern base reset.
